Compute
Match — Customer Guide (Find, Request and Track GPU Clusters)
This guide is for customers (also called Offtakers): organizations
that want to reserve GPU capacity from NVIDIA Cloud Providers
(NCPs).

Selecting clusters
Narrow the list with filters.
Click a map bubble or a card.

Step 2 — Fill the reservation
form
The form opens in a modal with three sections.
Cluster Details
Pre-filled and read-only when you picked a cluster.
With several clusters, they are shown as Option 1, Option 2…
separated by “or”, with an amber banner: these are
alternatives
, and your request will be matched with
one
cluster based on NCP availability.
For custom requests, GPU Model and Geographical Region are required
and Country is optional.

Custom requests (no
matching cluster)
If nothing fits, click
Submit a custom request
(banner under the filters) or
Submit Custom Request
(empty state). Your current filters are carried over as hints. A custom
request is not sent to a specific NCP; NVIDIA Platform Admins broker it
manually and move it through:
Open → In Review → Matched
or
Unserviceable
. You can cancel it while it is Open or In
Review. Custom requests never expire. You get an email at each step.
Step 3 — Track requests in
My Requests
Route:
/customer/reservations
.
Columns: Request ID (shown as “REQ-1 - Status”), Customer, Contact
Email, Platform, Geographical Region, Country, Requested GPUs, Total
GPUs, Requested Date, Start/End Date, Duration (Hours), Status.
Multi-NCP requests show as a grouped row with one child row per
NCP.
The date under the status chip is when it moved to In Process,
Contracted, Rejected, Expired or Cancelled. Rejected rows have an info
icon with the NCP’s remarks.
Filters: Status, Hosting Provider (hidden for multi-provider),
Platform, Geographical Region, Country, Sort by request date,
Clear All
.
With no requests you see
No requests found
with a
button to create one.
Step 4 — Reservation detail
Route:
/customer/reservations/{reservationId}
.
A headline states the status, for example “Your Reservation request
is awaiting NCP acceptance” or “Contract Complete!”, with the expiry
date when relevant.
Reservation Summary
: organization, contact email,
period, GPU count, platform, region, country, rejection remarks, terms
acceptance.
Proposal History
: every proposal (yours and NCP
counteroffers), grouped by region when several NCPs are involved.
Cancel
: available while Awaiting NCP Acceptance,
Awaiting Provider/Customer Approval, In Process or Expired. Confirm in
the modal; you may give a reason. All involved NCPs are notified by
email.
You cannot accept or reject NCP proposals on this page; the NCP
confirms the contract.
What happens after you
submit
You get a “request received” email.
Each selected NCP gets a magic-link email and has 7 days to
accept.
When an NCP accepts, the request goes
In Process
and you get an introduction email so you can negotiate directly. The
contract window is 45 days.
When an NCP clicks
Confirm Contract
, your request
becomes
Contracted
; other NCPs on the same request are
cancelled as superseded.
If every NCP rejects, the request is
Rejected
. If
all deadlines pass, it is
Expired
and you get one
consolidated expiry email.
Feedback
After creating a request you may see “How was the Request a Cluster
experience?” with 1-5 stars and
Submit Feedback
. When
cancelling or leaving the marketplace you may be asked why. You can also
click
Share Feedback
in the header at any time.
